dimensions.assessment: Affects public land users, local counties in Colorado (Dolores, San Miguel, Montezuma), agricultural water users, tribal members, grazing permit holders, and recreationists.
dimensions.evidence: The Conservation Area shall consist of approximately 52,872 acres of Bureau of Land Management land... Special Management Area shall consist of approximately 15,452 acres of Federal land in the San Juan National Forest

dimensions.assessment: Imposes sweeping land withdrawals from mining and mineral leasing, strict wilderness-like protections in Ponderosa Gorge, and specific multi-stakeholder management plans.

summary: S. 1787 establishes the Dolores River National Conservation Area and the Dolores River Special Management Area in Colorado. It outlines management requirements for these areas, protects existing water rights and tribal traditional uses, creates an advisory council, and releases certain river segments from further study under the Wild and Scenic Rivers System.

affected_groups.effect: Allowed continued use of the covered land for traditional ceremonies and as a source of traditional plants and other materials without altering treaty rights.
Protected existing water rights, water contracts, and operations of the Dolores Project and McPhee Reservoir, with representation on the advisory council.
affected_groups.group: Agricultural Water Users and Conservancy Districts

affected_groups.effect: The conservation and special management areas aim to protect recreational resources and whitewater boating values, with recreational representation on the advisory council.
Local counties such as Dolores, San Miguel, and Montezuma receive representation on the advisory council, and local road jurisdictions remain unaffected.
Permits and leases continue to be issued and administered in accordance with applicable laws governing BLM and Forest Service lands.

key_provisions: Establishes the Dolores River National Conservation Area consisting of approximately 52,872 acres of Bureau of Land Management land.
Establishes the Dolores River Special Management Area consisting of approximately 15,452 acres of federal land in the San Juan National Forest.
Requires the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture to develop long-term management plans for the respective areas within three years.
Establishes the Dolores River National Conservation Area Advisory Council with a 14-member board to advise on management plans.
Manages Ponderosa Gorge areas to maintain wilderness character by prohibiting new road construction, motor vehicles, mechanical transport, and commercial timber harvesting.
Releases designated segments of the Dolores River from further study for potential addition to the Wild and Scenic Rivers System.
Protects existing private water rights, state water jurisdiction, and the ongoing operation of the Dolores Project and McPhee Reservoir.
missing_information: Exact federal appropriations or specific financial costs required to implement the management plans and advisory council.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 1787 establishes the Dolores River National Conservation Area and the Dolores River Special Management Area in Colorado. It outlines management requirements for these areas, protects existing water rights and tribal traditional uses, creates an advisory council, and releases certain river segments from further study under the Wild and Scenic Rivers System.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts federal land management, water operations, and conservation rules across roughly 68,324 acres of public land in Colorado, while explicitly preserving existing private property rights, water decrees, and tribal privileges.
